retained_expressions_data_and_idioms: Exact public signatures and mediaType return property; no imports, additional exports, mutable shared state, or external dependency owners introduced.
Retained supplied protocol and delimiter data: data:, comma, semicolon, ==, and =. Repeated data: is factored into a private named constant.
Retained base64 numeric data: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, ASCII ranges 65..90, 97..122, 48..57, plus 43, slash 47, padding 61. Character codes and base64 group sizes use private named constants.
Retained native indexOf, slice, toLowerCase, split with limit 1, optional first-item trim, endsWith, length, charCodeAt, and Math.floor arithmetic.

Retained ordinary branching, conditional padding selection, range comparisons, sequential loops and object-literal return idioms. Exact static data and ordinary idioms are retained honestly; no novelty, license, grant, or clean-separation claim.

manual_review.method: Inspection of all six input contents and one full source read, without execution.
findings: parseDataUrlHeader calls indexOf before the prefix slice check, checks the prefix before the comma sentinel, retains optional trim and returns a fresh mediaType object only for a truthy trimmed header.
base64PayloadByteLength checks == before = and reads length only after suffix selection; floor arithmetic preserves the negative malformed = result.

isStrictBase64Payload preserves separate initial length reads, bypasses suffix reads for empty or non-multiple-of-four lengths, computes contentLength after padding selection, traverses each character in order, and checks remaining positions against ASCII 61 with a fresh length read per loop condition.
No padding-bit canonicalization, payload decoding, coercion, trimming beyond the first header item, MIME validation, or error wrapping added.
No own undefined keys are synthesized; native/getter errors remain uncaught.
Source is 78 lines, below the 400-line limit.
